title: Finite-free ramified coefficient stages without a geometric base
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and let $E\subseteq F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, equipped with their compatible extending absolute values. Let $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_F$, and let $t\in R$, $v\in S$ be uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Then $S$ is a finite free $R$-module. There are a unit $u\in S^\times$ and an integer $e\geq1$ such that $t=uv^e$. For every $n\geq1$, $t^nS=v^{en}S$, and the induced map $R/t^nR\to S/t^nS=S/v^{en}S$ is finite free. These are finite local rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$. The indices $en$ are cofinal in the positive integers, and the ideals and quotient maps are independent of unit changes in the chosen uniformizers.

proof.text: Use the coefficient convention [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] for each of $E$ and $F$. Thus $R,S$ are DVR domains with finite residue fields, their maximal ideals consist of the elements of absolute value less than $1$, and units have absolute value $1$. In particular $t,v$ are nonzero and have absolute value strictly between $0$ and $1$. Compatibility of the absolute values gives $R\subseteq S$ and preserves the absolute value of $t$. The inclusion is injective, and a unit of $R$ is a unit of $S$ since its inverse already belongs to $R$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis] to the given finite extensions $E\subseteq F$ with their compatible absolute values. Its hypotheses are exactly those here, with no geometric base. It supplies $b_1,\ldots,b_d\in S$, where $d=[F:E]$, such that every $s\in S$ has a unique expression $\sum_i a_i b_i$ with $a_i\in R$. This is a finite $R$-basis of $S$, proving finite freeness.

source.place: Part (1), coefficient-ring input, with ramified quotients expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] to the DVR $S$, its maximal-ideal generator $v$, and the nonzero element $t\in S$. The DVR hypothesis from Step 1 includes Noetherianity. Obtain $t=uv^e$ for a unit $u\in S$ and an integer $e\geq0$. If $e=0$, then $t=u$ would have absolute value $1$, contradicting $|t|<1$; hence $e\geq1$. For each $n\geq1$, $t^n=u^n v^{en}$ and $u^n$ is invertible, so $t^nS=v^{en}S$.

proof.text: For I=(t^n), identify S/IS with (R/I) tensor_R S using the quotient tensor equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], in its scalar-swapped Mathlib form Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor. Base change of a free finite module is free finite, and the linear equivalence transports these two properties. The algebra map is the canonical quotient map, sending [r] to [f(r)]. The private helper quotient_free_finite implements the base change and its scalar action explicitly.

proof.text: Rewrite (t^n) as m_R^n and (f(t)^n) as m_S^(e*n). The finite residue fields from [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] and Mathlib Ideal.finite_quotient_pow give finiteness, since each maximal ideal is generated by its uniformizer. Both quotient ideals are proper: a positive power of a nonunit remains a nonunit. Thus Mathlib IsLocalRing.of_surjective' applied to each quotient projection proves locality. For m<=n, Ideal.pow_le_pow_right and Ideal.Quotient.factor construct the transition maps, which send [x] to [x].

proof.text: By the p-adic norm formula [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] and the extending spectral absolute value [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], the image of l has absolute value less than one. The maximal-ideal characterization in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] therefore places l in m_R=(t). Applying f places l in (f(t)). Raising these ideal memberships to the nth power shows that l^n belongs to (t^n) and (f(t)^n), respectively. Hence both quotient rings are killed by l^n; take N=n. No additional unit-times-power factorization of l is needed.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, applied to the image of the coefficient prime

proof.text: For every positive integer $k$, choose $n=k$. Then $en\geq k$, and hence $v^{en}S\subseteq v^kS$; this proves the asserted cofinality. If $t$ is replaced by $t^{\prime}=a t$, $a\in R^\times$, and $v$ by $v^{\prime}=b v$, $b\in S^\times$, then $t^{\prime n}R=t^nR$, $t^{\prime n}S=t^nS$, and $v^{\prime j}S=v^jS$ for every $j$. Moreover $t^{\prime}=(a u b^{-e})(v^{\prime})^e$, with the coefficient again a unit of $S$, so the same cofinal exponents work. The quotient identifications are induced by the identity on $R$ or $S$. Every transition map sends the class of $x$ to the class of the same $x$, and every scalar map sends $[r]$ to $[r]$; consequently all these maps commute with the identifications. Thus independence concerns canonical quotient rings and their maps, not any chosen basis.
